summary: Set up automatic HTTPS certificate rotation on node1: nginx serves TLS on port 8443 using a certificate issued by a local CA, a renewal script (/usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh) reissues the leaf cert and gracefully reloads nginx (systemctl reload, no dropped connections), driven by a systemd timer (node1-cert-renew.timer, every 10 min, OnBootSec=2min) so renewal happens automatically well ahead of the cert's 24h validity and survives node restarts. Verified continuity under load during a live renewal (40/40 requests returned 200) and confirmed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-reboot boot_id/service health, rebooted node1, observed boot_id change, and confirmed nginx/timer came back active, served HTTPS 200, and the timer fired again post-reboot rotating the cert to a new serial while nginx kept answering.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via dnf
Created a local CA (/etc/pki/localca) and renewal script (/usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh) that issues a fresh short-validity leaf cert with NODE_IP/hostname SANs and gracefully reloads nginx
Configured nginx (/etc/nginx/conf.d/node1-https.conf) to listen on 8443 with TLS using the local CA cert/key, enabled and started nginx
Created systemd service+timer (node1-cert-renew.service/.timer) for automatic renewal every 10 minutes with OnBootSec=2min, enabled and started the timer
Manually triggered a renewal while running 40 concurrent HTTPS requests to prove zero downtime during cert rotation/reload
Verified served TLS cert serial matches the newly issued cert file after reload
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, service active states, live HTTP 200 check, cert serial/dates
Rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (910dc564... -> 4393f2d4...), proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart verified nginx and the renewal timer are active/enabled, HTTPS still serving 200, and waited for the timer's next scheduled fire to confirm automatic renewal resumed post-reboot (cert serial rotated again, nginx reloaded, still serving 200)

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with valid TLS handshake
evidence.summary: nginx listening on 8443 (IPv4/IPv6) and curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns 200

evidence.requirement: Certificate renewal mechanism issues a new certificate automatically
evidence.summary: systemd timer node1-cert-renew.timer fires the renewal script, which issues a new cert (serial changed 1790693041 -> 1790693063) well before the 24h expiry

evidence.requirement: Service picks up the new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: 40 concurrent HTTPS requests during a manual renewal+reload all returned 200; nginx journal shows graceful 'Reloading/Reloaded' with no downtime, and served cert serial (1790693071) matches the newly issued file

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (services, cert, boot identity)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, nginx/timer active, HTTPS 200, cert serial 1790693071 before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledged and executed (single node, non-destructive)
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled with ack returned before disconnect; subsequent exec calls timed out confirming the node went down for reboot

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id is 4393f2d4-86af-4261-8d83-52ed4c7b94b1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and exec connectivity was restored

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, HTTPS availability, and continued automatic renewal
evidence.summary: nginx and node1-cert-renew.timer active/enabled after reboot, HTTPS still returns 200, and the timer fired again post-reboot rotating the cert (serial 1790693071 -> 1790693219) while nginx served the new cert live with zero-downtime reload
